title: fix(driver-sql): removing a field default stores NULL on MySQL 8, and never leaves a NOT NULL column refusing writes
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8Jy8bxCRdEndf2kW8g6WXtd)_

Fixes #36596
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 修复 main 变红：字段删掉默认值后，MySQL 8 上不填该字段的新记录会被数据库拒绝，现在改为存空值，和 Postgres、SQLite 一致。
- 对「不允许为空」的列，删默认值不再单独执行：字段允许为空时和「放开非空」一起执行；字段仍要求非空时原样保留，只报出。
- 已有记录一行不改；改动可直接回退。

## The cause (premise correction)

The card says the dropped DEFAULT "leaves the column NOT NULL". Measured on MySQL 8.0.46, it does not: `digest` is `IS_NULLABLE = YES` throughout. The cause is MySQL 8's `ALTER COLUMN … DROP DEFAULT`, which leaves even a **nullable** column with no default at all, so a strict-mode insert that omits it fails with ER 1364 "Field 'digest' doesn't have a default value". `SET DEFAULT NULL` stores NULL. Round 1 (#36564) was measured on MariaDB 10.11, which stores NULL after `DROP DEFAULT`, and the live MySQL leg did not run on that PR.

```
mysql> CREATE TABLE p (id varchar(36) PRIMARY KEY, digest varchar(255) DEFAULT 'none');
mysql> ALTER TABLE p ALTER COLUMN digest DROP DEFAULT;
mysql> INSERT INTO p (id) VALUES ('a');
ERROR 1364 (HY000): Field 'digest' doesn't have a default value
mysql> ALTER TABLE p ALTER COLUMN digest SET DEFAULT NULL;
mysql> INSERT INTO p (id) VALUES ('a');   -- stores NULL
```

## What changes

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/**` only, plus this changeset.

- **MySQL `drop_column_default`** (`sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`): on a nullable column it is now `ALTER COLUMN … SET DEFAULT NULL`; a NOT NULL column keeps `DROP DEFAULT`. This also covers the #4560 token arm, which used the same statement.
- **A NOT NULL column with a stale literal DEFAULT** (`schema-drift.ts`): the drop never travels alone, because an omitting insert would then be refused.
  - When the declaration does not hold the column NOT NULL (the differ already proposes `relax_not_null`: `storage: { notNull: false }` in words, or no storage declaration on a non-`required` field), the drop is reported **with** that relax at the relax's category, `needs_confirm`. `os migrate apply` applies both; the publish and the managed package install (#33724) apply both when the field says `storage: { notNull: false }`. An unset insert then stores NULL. Dev auto-reconcile applies neither (ADR-0113 D5), so the column keeps storing the old default and is never left refusing writes.
  - Otherwise (`storage: { notNull: true }`, a `required` field, the ceremony-owned tenant column), the column is left alone. The entry is `destructive`, so no automatic or non-destructive path applies it, and it is warned at boot and listed by `os migrate plan`.
- `isPublishedColumnChange` / `isInstallRelaxation` select the paired drop alongside the declared relax (`isDeclaredRelaxPair`).

## Tests

`sql-driver-36245-stale-literal-default.test.ts`: §1 and §2 unchanged (not skipped, quarantined or narrowed); §2 now passes on live MySQL 8. New §3, per dialect cell (SQLite, live PG, live MySQL), on a NOT NULL column with `DEFAULT 'none'`:

1. No default, no storage declaration, not required: drift is `drop_column_default` + `relax_not_null`, both `needs_confirm`; dev boot leaves the column (unset insert stores `'none'`); `applyMigrationEntries` applies both; unset insert stores NULL; no drift after.
2. `storage: { notNull: false }`: `applyPublishedColumnChanges` applies both; unset insert stores NULL.
3. `storage: { notNull: true }`: one `destructive` entry; boot, publish and non-destructive apply leave the column NOT NULL with its default.
4. `required: true`, no storage: same as 3.

## Live PG + MySQL evidence (in-container, CI's own setup)

Servers: MySQL 8.0.46 (`STRICT_TRANS_TABLES`, `innodb_strict_mode=1`, `SET GLOBAL time_zone='+08:00'`) and PostgreSQL 16 (`ALTER SYSTEM SET timezone='Asia/Shanghai'`). Run exactly as the "Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)" step runs it: `TZ=America/New_York OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1 OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=… OS_TEST_MYSQL_URL=… pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql test`.

**Before (origin/main 79d9c143), the red reproduced on live MySQL 8:**

```
 FAIL  sql-driver-36245-stale-literal-default.test.ts > … #36245 §2 … (live mysql) > the second boot drops the removed default …
Error: insert into `os36245_pref` (`id`, `title`) values ('after', 'after') - Field 'digest' doesn't have a default value
 FAIL  sql-driver-36245-stale-literal-default.test.ts > … #36245 §2 … (live mysql) > without auto-reconcile the divergence is reported `safe` …
Error: insert into `os36245_pref` (`id`, `title`) values ('repaired', 'repaired') - Field 'digest' doesn't have a default value
```

**After (head f972c24c), the file, verbose:** 51 passed (51). Every §2 and §3 case passes on `sqlite`, `live postgres` and `live mysql` (18 two-boot cases, 6 per dialect); `driver-sql live-dialect coverage: all 3 dialects were exercised (sqlite, live postgres, live mysql)`.

**After, the whole driver-sql suite under the CI step's setup:**

```
 Test Files  1 failed | 280 passed | 1 skipped (282)
      Tests  1 failed | 7007 passed | 10 skipped (7018)
 FAIL  sql-driver-11565-row-byte-budget.test.ts > … row byte budget on live MySQL (#11565) > reports InnoDB page-limit refusals with the page limit, not the row budget
```

The one failure is not this PR's: it fails identically at origin/main 79d9c143 against the same local server (same command, main's `src/`), and passes on main's CI `mysql:8.0` image. The difference is this container's Ubuntu MySQL build, not the code: the case expects the server to refuse a new 40-column table, and this server accepts it. This PR touches no create path.

**Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to HEAD, run on all three cells):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| MySQL drop back to `DROP DEFAULT` on a nullable column | 4 fail: both §2 MySQL cases (ER 1364, the main-red failure), and the two MySQL §3 cases that relax then drop |
| NOT NULL column drop emitted `safe` and unpaired, as on main | 9 fail across all three dialects |
| Publish/install no longer select the paired drop | 3 fail: the `storage: { notNull: false }` publish case on each dialect |
| Pair the drop even when the declaration holds NOT NULL | 6 fail: the `notNull: true` and `required` cases on each dialect |

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (the publish paragraph under the drift-category table) says the publish applies "every `safe` column change, and a `relax_not_null` whose field declares `storage: { notNull: false }`". It now also applies the paired `drop_column_default`. That page is outside this card's file surface, so it is not edited here.
- On MySQL, `relax_not_null` runs `MODIFY … NULL`, which also drops a column's declared literal DEFAULT (measured: `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'x'` becomes `DEFAULT NULL`); the #36245 `set_column_default` arm restates it on the next sync. Pre-existing and unchanged here.
- The "Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)" job is path-filtered and skipped on PRs, which is how round 1 reached main. Making it run on a `driver-sql` PR is a `.github/workflows/ci.yml` change: governed (Tier H) and outside this card's file surface, so it is not made here. Evidence from in-container live servers is pasted instead.
